expected_return.window: scorebord: BUY 13:30 ET on the entry day; SELL amc at the next open, bmo at 13:00 ET on the report day; gross

note: Each member is reported as a percentile of its own live range, 0-100 (pct), with its direction in side; panel_pct (0-100) is the size of the mean of the signed percentiles and side its direction; panel_pct_sd their spread. The selection is panel_pct in the top 20%. panel_score is the signed median of the members' sizes, each read against its own recent history. consensus_k counts members that put the name in their own top 20% on the panel's side; that, not sign agreement, is what selected well on the development names. Certainty (p_up) is recorded and decides nothing. expected_edge_pct is a shrunk in-sample prior, not a forecast. Research only.

opus5.note: Two-sided and large: the permit-exclusive guide as a floor with consensus parked on it (item 0) plus a Chinese-language peer print showing InP volume AND price up (item 1) and a capacity raise that backlog corroborates (item 2), against a Q4 consensus of $77.45m sitting above the stated ~$60m/quarter capacity ceiling (item 3); sized only modestly positive because the -14.6 skew already pays for upside, so the long side is partly priced while the Q4-guide risk is not.

opus55.note: Rests on a permit-exclusive Q3 floor guide (item 0), Yunnan Germanium's InP price and volume strength reported only in Chinese (item 1), and an 18% short base (item 4). These are partly offset by the risk that the Q4 guide lands below the $77m consensus because of capacity and permits (item 3).

sonnet55.note: Rests on the Q3 guide being a permit-exclusive floor with consensus parked on it (item 0) and Yunnan Germanium's price/volume print (item 1), against Q4 guide risk at the capacity ceiling; the sealed skew already pays upside.

fable51.note: Rests on item 1 (Yunnan Germanium's Oct 20 Q3, after AXT last spoke, showing InP volume AND price rising, covered only in Chinese and not reflected in a stock that fell to $52 two days later) plus item 0 (a permit-exclusive guide the street has parked consensus exactly on) and item 2 (a subsidiary raise joined by a customer affiliate that funds a corroborated capacity ramp); the one real negative is item 3, a Q4 guide that may be set at permit-secured revenue below the $77m consensus, shrunk for an 18%-of-shares short with calls bid; abs_move above the 1-day straddle because the earnings-only history runs 8-29%.

opus5.note: Item 0 is the best thing on the day: arithmetic straight off the company's own releases shows H2 needs +16.2% while management guided case volume and price DOWN and EOS needs ~+48% half-on-half after two cuts, with FY consensus pinned at $882.06m (range $881.8-882.6m) so no trim is modelled — and this name's guidance-line surprises printed -31.7% and -22.3%; netted against the CEO's first open-market buy (item 1), which is a real counterweight on the quarter but not on the FY guide.

opus55.note: Rests on item 0: the company's own H2 arithmetic needs revenue to accelerate and EOS to step up, into a +22.5% run-up. The CEO's mid-quarter open-market buy (item 1) offsets part of that.

sonnet55.note: Rests on the H2 revenue-guide arithmetic (a $882m guide needs a +16% H2 acceleration while EOS has already been cut twice), offset by the CEO's $1m open-market buy mid-quarter and a 22% run-up.

fable51.note: Rests on item 0, the guide arithmetic from company documents (H2 must grow 16% and EOS must swing from -6% to +7% to hold $882m, with consensus pinned on the guide and a +22.5% run-up raising the bar) shrunk for a 7-days-to-cover short, against item 1, the CEO's first open-market buy ten weeks into the quarter, which argues no cut is coming and is mostly in the price at +37% since.

opus5.note: Rests on item 0: Q3 is the first quantified look at the unquantified claims-lag/SNF cost problem against a $20-30m EBITDA guide, on a name whose last three prints fell 20/10/6 and whose beats are sold; shrunk hard because the direction is already half-priced (-16% on Sept 15, PTs halved) and items 1 and 4 (benign peer MA trend, 2027 growth with competitors exiting) cut the other way.

opus55.note: Rests on item 0: the unquantified claims-lag cost trend and a likely FY EBITDA cut below $145m on a name that sells its beats. Benign MA peer prints (item 1) and 2027 growth (item 4) offset only part of it, so the lean is mild.

sonnet55.note: Rests on the unquantified Q3 cost trend and TD Cowen's H2 EBITDA cut against a $20-30m guide (item 0), partly offset by benign UNH/ELV peer prints and 2027 growth; this name sells its beats and the 3.5-star dollar hit is still unquantified.

fable51.note: Rests on item 0: the unquantified claims-lag and SNF cost pressure that gets its first number at this print against a $20-30m Q3 EBITDA guide and a FY guide TD Cowen already models below, on a name that sold its last three prints; the benign UNH/ELV MCRs (item 1) and the 2027 growth framing (item 4) are proxies that only partly offset, and the star-ratings quantification (item 3) is two-sided with a slight negative tilt.

opus5.note: Near a wash: the one document-backed mechanism is item 6 (Baillie Gifford's 5.4% stake to zero by 9/30 with Pale Fire absorbing 2.3m shares at $4.6-5.1, i.e. the seller that drove the slide to the low is finished) plus a 10.7%-of-float short at the 52-week low with calls bid, set against item 2, the enterprise NRR slide to 91% and the Q4/2027 dis-synergy framing, which is precisely the line that produced -14.7%, -11.6% and -12.9% on the last three prints; the beat case (items 0-1) is real but this name sells its beats.

opus55.note: Rests on several smaller positives at the 52-week low: a conservative revenue and EBITDA guide (items 0-1), a finished 5% seller absorbed by a 10.9% buyer (item 6), a 10.7% short with calls bid (item 5), and buyback capacity against a cash-heavy balance sheet (item 8). Falling enterprise NRR and the guide risk (item 2) hold it to a mild lean.

sonnet55.note: Revenue and EBITDA beats against a guide-midpoint consensus are offset by enterprise net retention falling to 91% and a history of six down prints in eight, so the net is near zero with a mild positioning lean up.

fable51.note: Rests on item 6 (Baillie Gifford's 5.4% stake sold to zero by 9/30 per 13G/A while Pale Fire bought to 10.9% at $4.6-5.1, a finished seller that explains the slide to the low) and item 5 (10.7%-of-float short at a 52-week low with calls bid), with the conservative-guide beat pattern (items 0-1) sized small because this name sold its last Q2 revenue and EBITDA beat by 15%; item 2, enterprise NRR at 91% and the Q4/2027 dis-synergy framing, is the live downside and lands on the line that drove the last three down-prints.

opus5.note: Small and negative: every item here is public and read by the whole street on the most-covered name in the universe, so the only thing with teeth is item 4 — the bar sits above Intel's own guide after seven straight guidance beats, the stock is up ~150% YTD, and the last two beat-and-raises printed -7.9% and -8.5% — reinforced by item 3's asymmetry, where a call silent on 14A names undercuts a story the market has already been handed; the server-supply (item 0) and 18A margin (item 6) positives are three months old and in the price.

opus55.note: Close to balanced. Server supply skewed into Q4 (item 0) is set against IDC's -20% PC units (item 1), a bar already above the guide on a name that sold its last beat-and-raise (item 4), and foundry hype the call may not confirm (item 3). The sealed baseline failed, so the scale is third-party.

sonnet55.note: Intel's own late-Q3/Q4 server supply skew points to a Q4 guide above the $16.9B consensus (item 0), but the bar sits above the guide, beats were sold in July 2026 and July 2025, and the baseline failed so there is no skew.

fable51.note: Near a non-result: item 0 (Intel's own July statement that server supply lands late Q3 and Q4 against a Q4 consensus only 3.5% above the Q3 midpoint) is offset by item 1 (IDC PC units -20% YoY, mostly inside the sub-seasonal guide but with unquantified Q4 channel-inventory risk) and item 4 (consensus and whisper already above the company guide on a name that sold its last two beat-and-raise prints); everything here is in wire copy for a mega-cap, and no sealed skew exists to lean on.
